Terminal interrupt and the only quit chord; IntelliJ has no quit chord and Ctrl+C is Copy there (#365)
TamboUI debug overlay; IntelliJ binds Ctrl+Shift+F12 to Hide All Tool Windows, which a terminal cannot deliver (#363)

Focus Editor hides every tool window island; IntelliJ's Hide All Tool Windows is Ctrl+Shift+F12, which is toggleDebugOverlay here (#363), so Focus Editor takes Ctrl+F11, an F-key with a Ctrl modifier that no profile binds (docs/keymap.md)
Double Shift needs key release events, which only the full Kitty keyboard mode sends and Vintelli does not enable; Ctrl+P is the command palette stand-in
F1 is not on the IntelliJ default keymap page (it lists Ctrl+F1 for Error Description and Ctrl+Q for Quick Documentation); here it opens the keymap help
Opens the shell menu; no IntelliJ chord confirmed against the reference page
Focus the navigation bar; no IntelliJ chord confirmed against the reference page
New project file; IntelliJ binds F7 to Step Into in the debugger, and no New File chord is confirmed here
New project directory; IntelliJ binds F9 to Resume Program, and no new-directory chord is confirmed here
Rename in the project pane; F2 is Next Highlighted Error in IntelliJ, so F2 moved to the editor action
Deletes the project entry; no IntelliJ chord confirmed; shares Delete with deleteForward, the pane scope decides
Refreshes the project tree; IntelliJ's F5 is Synchronize in the project view, not confirmed against the reference page
Reveals the open file in the project pane (crosshair); the nearest IntelliJ chord, since IntelliJ's Alt+F1 opens the Select In list instead
Expand All is Ctrl+Shift+NumPad + in IntelliJ, which a Kitty-capable terminal sends as its own chord; F4 stays as the fallback for terminals without the Kitty keyboard protocol
Collapse All is Ctrl+Shift+NumPad - in IntelliJ, which a Kitty-capable terminal sends as its own chord; Alt+C stays as the fallback for terminals without the Kitty keyboard protocol
Pane header view menu; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
Pane header New menu; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
Pane header options menu; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
IntelliJ toggles the Project window with Alt+1, which is ActivateProjectToolWindow here (#364); Alt+P hides the pane
Opens the selected file in the project pane; no IntelliJ chord confirmed; shares Enter with confirm and select, the focus decides
IntelliJ Save All is Ctrl+S; our action saves the open file
Undo
Redo is Ctrl+Shift+Z in IntelliJ, which a Kitty-capable terminal sends as its own chord; Ctrl+Y stays as the fallback for terminals without the Kitty keyboard protocol (docs/keymap.md)
Find
Cut the selection to the clipboard; with no selection it reports that nothing is selected
Copy the selection; in the editor Ctrl+C quits only when no text is selected (see docs/keymap.md)
Paste from the clipboard, replacing the selection
Duplicate Line; with a selection it duplicates the caret line only and clears the selection, IntelliJ duplicates the selected text (docs/keymap.md)
Select All; the vim profile uses Ctrl+E because Ctrl+A is the Vim increment (docs/keymap.md)
Closes the editor tab; Ctrl+W is Extend Selection in IntelliJ, so it is not bound here
Select Next Tab
Select Previous Tab
Go to Declaration; F12 is Jump to Last Tool Window in IntelliJ, so F12 is left unbound (#366)
Find Usages
Folds or unfolds imports; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
Toggle Line Breakpoint; Ctrl+B is Go to Declaration
Edits the condition of the breakpoint on the caret line; IntelliJ offers conditions only from its gutter menu
Next Highlighted Error; the bare F2 trigger refuses Shift, and F8 is left unbound (docs/keymap.md)
Previous Highlighted Error on its own Shift+F2 trigger (docs/keymap.md)
Quick fixes from the language server for the selection or caret, offered in a popup (docs/keymap.md)
Extract Variable from the selection through the language server; a legacy terminal does not send Ctrl+Alt+letter, so the command palette runs it there (docs/keymap.md)
Extract Method from the selected statements through the language server; the Ctrl+Alt+letter limit of Extract Variable applies (docs/keymap.md)
Extract Constant from the selection through the language server; the Ctrl+Alt+letter limit of Extract Variable applies (docs/keymap.md)
Code completion from the language server at the caret, offered in a popup; Ctrl+@ is the NUL spelling of the same key that some terminals send (docs/keymap.md)
Quick documentation of the symbol at the caret from the language server, in a popup beside the caret (docs/keymap.md)
Generate from the language server's source actions for the class at the caret, in a popup beside the caret; the vim profile binds no chord (docs/keymap.md)
Reformats the file, or only the selected lines, with the language server's formatter (docs/keymap.md)
Runs the language server's organize imports action, which removes unused imports and sorts the rest (docs/keymap.md)
Rename Symbol in the editor: renames the symbol and its references through the language server; Shift+F6 keeps renaming the project entry while the project pane has focus (docs/keymap.md)
Move Caret to Previous Word; the editor text area takes it under the Kitty keyboard protocol
Move Caret to Next Word; the editor text area takes it under the Kitty keyboard protocol
Deletes the word before the caret in the editor under the Kitty keyboard protocol; no IntelliJ chord is confirmed on the reference page for this action
Deletes the word after the caret in the editor under the Kitty keyboard protocol; no IntelliJ chord is confirmed on the reference page for this action
Go to File is Ctrl+Shift+N in IntelliJ, which a Kitty-capable terminal sends as its own chord; Ctrl+O stays as the fallback for terminals without the Kitty keyboard protocol (docs/keymap.md)
Find in Files is Ctrl+Shift+F in IntelliJ, which a Kitty-capable terminal sends as its own chord; Alt+F stays as the fallback for terminals without the Kitty keyboard protocol
Go to Line with the IntelliJ chord; the vim profile binds Alt+G instead (docs/keymap.md)
Go to Class with the IntelliJ chord; Ctrl+Shift+N stays Go to File, so the unshifted chord is bound (docs/keymap.md)
Go to Symbol with the IntelliJ chord, which needs the Kitty keyboard protocol; tmux and ghostty may intercept it, and the palette and the Navigate menu reach it (docs/keymap.md)
Widens the project panel; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
Narrows the project panel; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
Grows the bottom tool window; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
Shrinks the bottom tool window; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
Switches the shell theme; Ctrl+T is Update Project in IntelliJ and stays here as the theme switch (docs/keymap.md)
Opens the debugger inspection window
IntelliJ uses Alt+F12 for Terminal (#364); Alt+2 stays as a second binding because the owner kept it, and the bare 2 is the shortcut while no input has focus
IntelliJ gives Maven no number; 9 is a number IntelliJ gives Version Control, which we do not have (#364)
IntelliJ gives no number to ACP Agents; 8 is a number IntelliJ gives Services, which we do not have (#364)
Open Settings is Ctrl+Alt+S in IntelliJ; it opens from the toolbar and the palette, and no chord is bound here yet
Connects to a running IntelliJ IDEA; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page
Run is Shift+F10 in IntelliJ; unbound here, the toolbar and the palette start the selected configuration
Debug is Shift+F9 in IntelliJ; unbound here, the toolbar and the palette start the debug session
Stop is Ctrl+F2 in IntelliJ; unbound here, the palette stops the current run
Refreshes the run configurations; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page
Chooses the run configuration; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page
Resume Program is F9 in IntelliJ; F9 is New Directory in the project pane, so the debugger keeps its own keys
Pause Program is not on the IntelliJ reference page; the debugger keeps its own keys
Step Over is F8 in IntelliJ; F8 stays free for the debugger work (docs/keymap.md)
Step Into is F7 in IntelliJ; F7 is New Project File in the project pane
Step Out is Shift+F8 in IntelliJ; unbound here, the debugger work decides

Set Value is F2 in IntelliJ; F2 sets the value only while the Debug window holds the keyboard (a window key like e for Evaluate), because the keymap keeps F2 on Next Problem, so the palette runs the action
Runs the typed command in the terminal window; IntelliJ has no chord for it

Refreshes the problems; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page for the Problems window

Selects the previous row of the window; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page for the Problems window
Shows all problems; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page for the Problems window
Shows only the problem errors; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page for the Problems window
Shows only the problem warnings; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page for the Problems window
